subtype: Approach: confront the colleague in anger [Pitfall]
passage:
I was three desks away when Sahil found out about the payments. He read the spreadsheet, went white, then stormed across the open office and said loudly to Rohit, "You've been cooking these numbers, haven't you?"

Everyone stopped typing. Rohit said nothing, just looked at the floor. Over lunch, though, I noticed his monitor was dark and his drive folder was almost empty. By evening two teammates had stopped speaking to Sahil, and one whispered that he had ruined someone's career on a hunch.

I'm Madhuri. I can't tell whether Sahil was furious or scared, maybe both. I do know that a quiet report with the files intact would have been much harder to brush off.

qa.q: What happened to Rohit's drive folder by lunch?
qa.a: It was almost empty, and his monitor was dark.

qa.q: What might Sahil have been feeling when he crossed the office to speak to Rohit?
qa.a: Sahil was probably angry and shocked, though Madhuri admits it might also have been fear, which is why the outburst came so fast.

qa.q: What could Sahil have done instead of confronting Rohit, and why would it work better?
qa.a: Sahil could have saved a copy of what he found and taken it privately to the right person, because the evidence would stay intact and no one would be warned.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt in the open office?
qa.a: Rohit likely felt exposed and cornered, with everyone watching, which makes hiding the files a frightened first move rather than a considered one.

grounding: Upset by a discovery, a person accuses a colleague in an open office, files vanish and the team turns hostile.

subtype: Approach: confront the colleague in anger [Pitfall]
passage:
Monday. Ishita, three months into the accounts team, finds that Abhinav's expense claims include hotel bills for a conference that, according to the event's own website, was cancelled. Her face goes hot. She hardly sleeps that night.
Tuesday, 10 a.m. She walks to Abhinav's desk in the open office with printouts in her hand. 'You claimed hotels for a cancelled conference. That's stealing.' Everyone stops typing. Abhinav's face goes red. 'You don't know anything. Get away from my desk.' By lunch, two colleagues have stopped talking to her.
Thursday. When internal audit finally asks for the claim files, the scanned hotel bills on the shared drive are gone. Abhinav says he 'cleaned up old folders'. The auditor tells Ishita there is now very little to check. She sits alone in the canteen, wishing she had taken her printouts quietly to the compliance officer on Monday instead of to his desk.

qa.q: What did Ishita say at Abhinav's desk?
qa.a: 'You claimed hotels for a cancelled conference. That's stealing.'

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling on Monday night?
qa.a: Angry and upset, her face hot, too stirred up to sleep.

qa.q: What could Ishita have done on Monday instead?
qa.a: Taken the printouts quietly to the compliance officer, so the files could be secured before anyone was alerted.

qa.q: How might the colleagues who stopped talking to Ishita see the scene?
qa.a: They saw a public accusation, felt uncomfortable or loyal to Abhinav, and turned against her without knowing the facts.

grounding: Shows an employee angrily accusing a colleague in the open office, after which files are deleted and the team turns hostile.

subtype: Approach: confront the colleague in anger [Pitfall]
passage:
Keerthana, you're angry. Good, you should be. But before you walk into that office tomorrow, let your Avni chithi tell you about the worst day of my first job.
I was twenty-one, at a trading company in Madurai. I found out a senior colleague was entering fake sales to earn a bonus. I was so angry my hands shook. And instead of taking the ledger to the owner, I stood in the middle of the office and shouted it at him, in front of everyone.
He shouted back. By evening half the office was on his side; they thought I was a young show-off. That night the pages I had marked in the ledger went missing. When the owner finally asked, I had nothing to show but my word.
I left three months later. He stayed two more years.
The anger was right, Keerthana. Where I put it was wrong. Write it down, keep the evidence, and take it quietly to the right person.

qa.a: At a trading company in Madurai.

qa.q: How did young Avni feel on discovering the fake sales?
qa.a: So angry her hands shook, which pushed her into shouting instead of planning.

qa.q: Which choice in the story could have kept the evidence safe?
qa.a: Taking the ledger quietly to the owner instead of confronting the colleague in front of everyone.

qa.q: How might the office staff have seen young Avni that day?
qa.a: As a young show-off making a scene, which turned them to the colleague's side without looking at the facts.

grounding: Shows a young employee confronting a colleague in anger in front of the office, after which evidence vanishes and colleagues turn hostile.
